subject: Pilot MAP and SLA tradeoffs — Nimbus pilot
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Jane Carroll <jane@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot MAP & proposed SLA terms for Nimbus pilot

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we think will fit Nimbus's evaluation window and pilot needs. High-level ask: 4–6 week evaluation to validate latency and throughput on your real queries, with a production ramp plan contingent on hitting milestone SLOs.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Week 0: Kickoff, access provisioned (VPC peering + sample dataset)
- Week 1–2: Baseline run, observability hooks, collect p50/p95 latency and token throughput
- Week 3: Tuning — batching, quantization profile, model variant selection
- Week 4: Final acceptance run + performance verification; decision to sign and commit

Commercial tradeoffs we propose:
- If Nimbus signs a 12‑month committed spend (minimum $480k ARR), Redwood will guarantee tightened latency SLOs for the production route and provide a ramp discount schedule.
- SLA: p95 latency target 400ms for the main inference route (defined at 1K prompt tokens). SLA credit structure attached.
- If SLA missed for two consecutive weekly windows after go‑live, Nimbus receives service credits up to 15% of monthly invoice (see attached sla_credit_table.csv).

Attachments: Nimbus_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP detail), redwood_rate_card_q2.xlsx (rates + committed discount tiers), sla_credit_table.csv (credit table and measurement method).

Can you confirm the evaluation window you want and whether the 12‑month commit + tightened SLA for credits is something your procurement team would entertain? Happy to jump on 30 minutes to walk through.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Jane Carroll <jane@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Erin Matthews <erin@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & proposed SLA terms for Nimbus pilot

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the clear MAP. A couple of clarifying questions from our side:
1) On the p95 400ms target — our production expectations for the user flow require tighter latency. For the same 1K token envelope, can Redwood commit to p95 250ms for the primary inference route if we sign a 12‑month commitment?
2) How is the SLA measured (client‑side vs infra-side)? We need the measurement to be server-side with shared dashboards.
3) For ramp discounts, can you confirm the discount at $480k vs $720k?

Procurement will also ask for a failure allowance. The SLA credits look reasonable but need to confirm with legal.

We can do the 4‑6 week evaluation but would like to shorten to 3 weeks if we can agree on acceptance criteria up front. Can you share the acceptance test suite you expect to run?

—Jane
Jane Carroll
Head of Platform — Nimbus Analytics
jane@nimbus-analytics.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Jane Carroll <jane@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & proposed SLA terms for Nimbus pilot

Jane —

Appreciate the specificity. Short answers up front:
- We can tighten to p95 250ms as a special commercial concession, conditional on a 12‑month minimum commitment at the $720k ARR tier and a three‑week evaluation with the acceptance suite run in Week 2.
- SLA is measured at the server edge (Redwood's telemetry) with shared dashboards. We'll push read‑only dashboards to your team for the evaluation and on‑go live.
- Discount tiers: $480k ARR = 12% discount; $720k ARR = 18% discount. Details in the attached rate card.

Proposed acceptance criteria (high level):
- Week 1 baseline: p50, p95, and error rate established
- Week 2 tuning: fixed config and run acceptance suite (shared test harness link) — acceptance if p95 <= 250ms and error rate < 0.2% over a 24h window
- Week 3 burn: stability check and rollout planning

If you can confirm the commitment tier, we'll update the MAP and prepare a DocuSign packet that includes the SLA appendix with credit triggers.

I'll loop in Legal/Contracts if you want a pre‑review.

Thanks,
Olga
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Nimbus MAP - SLO vs discount tradeoffs

Quick internal note before we send the updated MAP to Nimbus and legal:
- IFR: moving to p95 250ms materially increases reserved capacity requirements for their peak profile (their bursts are 3x baseline). We should gate the concession on a 12‑month commit at the $720k ARR tier and include a throughput ramp schedule to protect capacity (e.g., week 1 max 30% of committed QPS, week 2 60%, week 3 100%).
- Request that Contracts include a clause that allows Redwood to rely on measured server-side telemetry and exclude customer-induced misconfigurations (network issues, malformed prompts) from SLA calculations.
- Prepare a fallback: if we cannot meet the p95 for the 1K token envelope, provide a model-variant fallback (slightly cheaper latency optimized model) and apply a partial credit schedule.

I'll draft suggested language for the DocuSign SLA appendix.
Neha
Head of Customer Solutions (acting)
From: Erin Matthews <erin@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Jane Carroll <jane@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Apr 2027 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & proposed SLA terms for Nimbus pilot

Olga/Jane —

Legal has reviewed the terms. A few requested modifications:
- We need the SLA measurement to be mutually agreed metrics; please include a table that defines the measurement point and the exact aggregation window (we prefer 5‑min rolling window, then weekly p95).
- Add an exception carve‑out for force majeure and scheduled maintenance with >48h notice.
- For credits: we need a cap per incident (30% of monthly invoice) and an annual aggregate cap (no more than 25% annual credits).

If Redwood accepts these three edits, we're prepared to move to DocuSign. Please send the updated appendix.

Thanks,
Erin
Senior Counsel — Nimbus Analytics
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Jane Carroll <jane@nimbus-analytics.com>, Erin Matthews <erin@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & proposed SLA terms for Nimbus pilot

Erin/Jane —

Thanks — we can accept the measurement table (we'll attach the exact measurement table in the appendix), the force majeure and scheduled maintenance carveouts, and the credit caps you requested (cap per incident 30%, annual cap 25%). Those will be reflected in the DocuSign SLA appendix.

Next steps:
1) I attached the updated MAP and rate card in this thread.
2) I'll upload the DocuSign packet (includes finalized SLA appendix) and share the link here within the hour.
3) Nimbus to sign + kickoff within 48 hours of signature, evaluation runs immediately after.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/sign/XYZ123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/NIM-2027-042

Appreciate the speed — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Olga
